claims.wording: Selective, grounded event-argument extraction on RAMS: QLoRA sharply improved grounding, and no system — QLoRA, few-shot or zero-shot — could be certified at the frozen risk target. An evidence-first negative result.
claims.scope: the GitHub repository description field — one line, no second passage
claims.method: Authored for the one-line constraint rather than compressed from an existing claim, because render_surface emits limitations as sub-bullets and a single-string field can carry none. It is the conjunction of CX-GROUNDING-01 (a large improvement in grounding fidelity, stated qualitatively) and CX-H1-PRIMARY plus CX-H2-SECONDARY (no system certified), held in one clause because the claim boundaries require the grounding gain and the null to appear in the same passage. THE DESCRIPTION ITSELF QUOTES NO FIGURE, deliberately - see its wording above, which carries none. The grounding rate is forbidden outside a passage carrying the null, and the ungrounded-span ratio belongs to CX-GROUNDING-ORTHOGONAL-01 and is licensed only with the restricted-population caveat attached, which a one-line surface cannot carry. The first draft of the description quoted that ratio, cited it to the wrong claim, and mis-stated what it measured: it is the reduction in UNGROUNDED SPANS, recorded in CX-GROUNDING-01, not the change in the GROUNDING RATE, which is a smaller multiple. Both figures are stated in CX-GROUNDING-01 and neither is restated here.
limitations: In-domain RAMS only, at the frozen operating point (alpha 0.20, delta 0.05, acceptance floor 0.20), on the frozen vLLM 4-bit serving stack. None of that fits in the field, which is why the field must not be read as the claim's scope.
The null is ALL THREE systems, not a QLoRA-versus-baseline comparison. H1 and H2 collapse to one finding and no numerical difference is computed against an infeasible baseline.
"Improved grounding" means parseable-and-grounded output, NOT correctness. It must never be read as accuracy.

"Could not be certified" is not a near miss. Under an oracle with no finite-sample penalty the best system accepts 2.0% against a required 20%, and below alpha ~0.406 no certificate at any threshold could clear the floor.

This field is the whole claim for most of its readers. It is rendered in search results and link previews where nothing else in the repository is present, so it must be judged as though nothing behind it will be read.

claims.wording: The infeasibility has two separable causes and only the first is a capability gap. (1) CAPABILITY, specific to this model and score on this task: with an unlimited threshold grid, no finite-sample penalty and oracle threshold selection, the adapted system accepts at most 2.0% of documents at 20% empirical error, where a perfect ranking of the same population reaches 23.6%. Both figures are empirical and penalty-free, so the 21.6-point gap is attributable to the score and not to the coarse grid, the delta split, the bound looseness or a distribution difference between splits. (2) METHOD AND BENCHMARK, independent of capability: at n = 1,396 groups with delta/3, a Hoeffding bound spends 0.0925 of the 0.20 risk budget on the finite-sample penalty before any data is seen - a DIAGNOSTIC pairing belonging to neither certifier construction, since the primary risk test is empirical Bernstein and the conservative audit ran Hoeffding at a single candidate on the full delta. Under that diagnostic, passing the RISK test at exactly the 20% acceptance floor (k = 280) requires mean loss at most 0.1075 - barely half the nominal target - whoever produced it; that is the risk test's requirement under one bound, not what every certificate requires, since the primary test's requirement depends on the loss distribution. For this model the outcome is settled independently of the score and of the bound: at the frozen allocation acceptance needs at least 332 groups, and the loss-optimal 332-group prefix, which no score can beat, already averages 0.2012 loss, above the target (under the Hoeffding diagnostic the loss-optimal ranking certifies 0.1139 at delta/3, below the floor). Separately, at delta/3 this corpus admits at most a three-candidate grid, which the frozen configuration exactly fills.
claims.scope: in-domain RAMS; (1) oracle risk-coverage diagnostic on the certification and development splits, (2) the frozen n = 1,396 corpus at alpha = 0.20, delta/3 and a 20% acceptance floor
claims.method: (1) Oracle risk-coverage frontier over source-document groups via certification_run.risk_coverage_frontier, using the same aggregation, eligibility, loss and score as the certifier; no threshold is selected or certified. (2) A Hoeffding upper bound (certification.hoeffding_upper, a diagnostic pairing rather than either certifier's construction) at certified_delta = delta/3, via calibration.acceptance_certified_loss_optimal (the loss-sorted prefix, which weakly dominates every score-induced ordering at every k) and certification.largest_scorc_grid at n = 1,396. Each figure is stamped with its delta, allocation, candidate count and n in the artifact that carries it - 0.0925, 0.1075 and k = 280 in evidence/plan3/derived_quantities.json, 0.1139 in evidence/plan3/calibration_diagnostics.json, and the acceptance lower bound and grid capacity in evidence/plan3/certification_sensitivity.json. An earlier wording named the sensitivity artifact for all of them and it carried two. NOTE THE CONSTRUCTION: 0.0925 is a Hoeffding radius at the per-system delta/3, a DIAGNOSTIC pairing - the primary certificate's risk test is empirical Bernstein and the conservative audit ran Hoeffding with a single candidate at the full delta, so 0.0925 is neither construction's own number.
limitations: A diagnostic, not a certificate: it selects no threshold and certifies nothing.
The same oracle diagnostic on the development split gives 3.0%, so cause (1) reproduces out of sample.

Cause (1) is specific to this model, this confidence score and this task. It is not evidence that event-argument extraction, or structured extraction generally, cannot be certified at 20% risk: 2606.29054's own datasets include base risks of 0.033 and 0.356, at which the arithmetic bound forbids nothing and permits up to 80.5% acceptance respectively (docs/frontier-check/findings.md, re-verified 2026-07-22).

Cause (2) is NOT the claim that no model could be certified on this corpus. The witness has to clear BOTH tests, and the one first offered here did not: mean loss at most 0.1075 over an accepted 20% clears the risk test at n = 1,396 and delta/3 while its Clopper-Pearson acceptance lower bound is 0.16566, so that system is NOT certified. The corrected witness is stated at the smallest prefix that clears acceptance, k = 332: there the acceptance lower bound is 0.2004 and the Hoeffding radius 0.0849, so a system carrying mean loss at most 0.1151 over its 332 best-ranked groups would pass both tests under that Hoeffding diagnostic. Under the primary empirical-Bernstein test the condition depends on the loss distribution, not the mean alone: an independent review found a constant-loss set of that size at 0.1151 certifies while a 0/1 set at a slightly lower mean does not (evidence/plan3/reviewer_record.c1-2026-08-03-packets.json), and a zero-loss set certifies under either. Clearing one of two constraints is not a counter-example to infeasibility. What cause (2) establishes is that, under the Hoeffding diagnostic at this allocation, the corpus halves the risk test's effective target for every system, and that for THIS model no score whatsoever clears what remains.

The two causes attach to different mechanisms of the three-way decomposition and must not be merged: cause (1) is ranking (mechanism 2), cause (2) is the finite-sample penalty (mechanism 3) plus grid capacity. Base risk (mechanism 1) belongs to neither - it settles ZS and FS outright and permits QA 49.1%.

Narrowed 2026-08-03. This claim previously read 'a capability gap rather than a limitation of the certification method' and attributed BOTH causes to capability, which is the same flattering direction as the five quoting errors recorded in the write-up's limitations, expressed in attribution rather than in arithmetic.

The Hoeffding figures in cause (2) use the conservative TWO-SIDED constant; the tight one-sided radius at k = 280 and delta/3 is about 8% smaller (certification.hoeffding_upper docstring). 'Barely half the nominal target' therefore slightly overstates the penalty, in the direction that strengthens cause (2), and is disclosed here for that reason.
claims.verified_by: conformalextract risk-coverage-diagnostic; reviewer re-derived 2.01% independently through the implementer's own aggregation, 2026-07-22

claims.wording: The adapted system's outputs are stack-dependent: the vLLM 4-bit serving stack and the transformers training stack agree on 86.3% of frames under greedy decoding, and 40 of 41 disagreements change the predicted content.
claims.method: Standalone transformers+peft regeneration compared against the served vLLM outputs, with prompt reproduction verified by sha256 on all 300.
limitations: Measured on train-split frames only; the rate may differ on other splits.
Divergence is quality-neutral against gold and concentrates in low-confidence frames.
No threshold was pre-registered for this probe, so 86.3% is reported, not judged as a pass.

The abstain/extract decision itself flips between stacks on 1.33% of frames at full acceptance (4 of 300) and on 1.78% under tightening (the SAME four flips over the top-75% denominator, 4 of 225). These are two measurements of different things, not an interval: an earlier wording printed them as '1.3-1.8%', which reads as a confidence interval and asserts a sampling uncertainty neither figure carries. Both values are correct, so no value check could see the defect - the form was wrong, not the number. Two of the four flips sit just above the median confidence percentile, so at plausible operating points (above about 50% acceptance) they survive into the accepted set rather than being abstained away: the abstention mechanism is stack-dependent at the margin.

The reassurance in limitation 2 is operating-point-dependent and must not be carried forward alone: at top-90% acceptance divergence is 12.59%, barely below the 13.67% raw rate. The near-zero top-quartile result holds only under aggressive abstention.
The top-quartile concentration result is 0 of 75, which is not zero: it carries a two-sided Clopper-Pearson 95% upper bound of 4.80%. Quote the bound whenever the concentration is quoted.
The CAUSE of the divergence is not isolated to a specific kernel, quantisation path or sampler. Nothing about it may be assumed fixed by changing any one of them.

claims.wording: QLoRA sharply improved output validity and span grounding for event-argument extraction on RAMS, but did not make low-risk documents identifiable using transition-logprobability confidence: the adapter's ~16x reduction in ungrounded spans over the baselines moved the certifiable frontier by 0.017 for itself and by 0.000 for both baselines, because 87% of its remaining loss sits in output that is well-formed, grounded and content-bearing, and is scored wrong anyway.
claims.scope: in-domain RAMS certification split, 1,396 source-document groups, frozen vLLM 4-bit serving stack
claims.method: Document loss decomposed into four channels (structural failure, grounding failure, valid-but-contentless, valid content-bearing); group-level channel contributions sum exactly to the unweighted mean of group means the certificate bounds under ADR 0009. Counterfactual: each system re-scored over content-bearing documents only, coverage measured against the restricted population. For the baselines the conclusion rests on an arithmetic ceiling rather than the counterfactual: accepting a fraction c at risk alpha requires population mean loss at most alpha*c + (1-c) = 0.84, and their restricted mean losses are 0.984 and 0.951.
limitations: This is a DISSOCIATION, not an orthogonality or independence result, and the wording was narrowed to say so on 2026-08-02. One intervention observed across three systems cannot establish that two properties are independent; what is measured is that a large gain in the first produced almost none in the second. Any reading as statistical independence, or as a general relationship between grounding and certifiability, exceeds this evidence.

The claim identifier still contains the word ORTHOGONAL. It is retained only so that the reviewer records which ruled on this claim remain traceable to it; the identifier is historical and the claim no longer asserts orthogonality.
Descriptive only: the decomposition and the grounding-oracle counterfactual select no threshold and certify nothing.
Conditional coverage under the grounding oracle is not a deployable acceptance rate and is not comparable across systems; the restricted population differs per system.

The restriction is NOT uniformly generous: it raises the loss of 24 few-shot and 21 QLoRA groups, and a correctness-oracle variant moves the baselines off zero. The baselines' result is carried by the arithmetic ceiling, not by the counterfactual.
The QLoRA system sits below that ceiling, so for it the ceiling is silent and only the measured curve leaves it short of the floor.
Scoped to in-domain RAMS under span-exact matching and to the frozen vLLM 4-bit serving stack (86.3% parsed-output parity); portability is not established.
The certificate bounds average within-group loss, not the absence of error in any document (ADR 0009).

The decomposition locates loss by CHANNEL; it does not identify the error category that produced it, and this claim no longer asserts one. Until 2026-07-29 the wording said the residual loss was output 'that names the wrong entity' — an attribution whose only source was ADR 0007's unquantified inspection of two development examples, which plan section 12.3 forbids generalising from. Removed on independent review (evidence/plan3/reviewer_record.plan3-close.json, finding O2).

A measurement points the other way and is recorded here rather than left in the review. On QA's content-bearing certification frames: tp 2,984, fp 4,434, fn 3,797 — false positives EXCEED false negatives by 637 arguments, i.e. systematic over-generation, which is not an entity-naming error. 2,003 of 2,515 error-bearing documents show both fp and fn, consistent with substitution, so 'mostly missing arguments' is ruled out. Wrong-role, boundary and coreference errors share that signature. Plan section 12.1's machine-coded taxonomy is what would separate them; it was descoped from Plan 3 on 2026-10-27 (disposition Amendment 2, ruled acceptable by the independent delta review in evidence/plan3/reviewer_record.plan3-close-chain-delta.json) rather than run, so no error-category claim is made.

Directional, and specific to the adapted system: on the same channel and the same frozen scorer, the two baselines run the OTHER way - they under-generate where QA over-generates. Normalised per document in the content-bearing channel, the excess of false positives over false negatives is +0.224 for QA against -1.168 for zero-shot and -1.328 for few-shot. The figures must be read per document and not as raw counts: the content-bearing channel is defined per system and the baselines reach it on far fewer documents (2,847 for QA against 1,238 and 1,130), so the channel filter alone would make raw totals incomparable. What survives normalisation is the SIGN, which is the whole of the claim.
claims.verified_by: evidence/plan3/reviewer_record.reanalysis.json (independent review, 2026-07-22: numbers CONFIRMED by from-scratch recomputation; BLOCK on six discipline/wording items, all corrected)

claims.wording: On the oracle risk-coverage curve, the 20% acceptance floor first becomes reachable at a target risk of about 0.406 for the QLoRA system, 0.930 for few-shot and 0.981 for zero-shot. These are EMPIRICAL ORACLE FRONTIER points measured on an already-opened split, not thresholds and not certified operating points. Across the whole range below them no selective policy at any threshold could have cleared the floor, so the infeasibility at the frozen 0.20 target is not an artefact of that particular choice; it holds across everything up to twice it.
claims.scope: in-domain RAMS certification split, 1,396 source-document groups; oracle upper bound (the development split is reported in the same artifact and agrees, at 0.383 for the QLoRA system)
claims.method: The oracle risk-coverage curve carries no target risk; max acceptance at a given target is that fixed curve read at one height. No certificate is issued at any point on the curve; the frozen target of 0.20 is unchanged (ADR 0007).
limitations: 0.406 is an empirical oracle frontier point, not a threshold and not a certified operating point. It was computed AFTER the certification split was opened, from the labels of that split, so it describes where this measured population's curve crosses the floor and nothing more. Calling it a threshold would imply a certificate that was never issued at it or at any other point.
An oracle upper bound with no finite-sample penalty, no grid and no multiplicity correction: usable only to rule operating points out, never to indicate that a weaker one would certify.

The crossing is a necessary condition, not a sufficient one. A certificate at 0.406 would not issue: at the ~280 groups a 20% acceptance implies, the Hoeffding radius alone is 0.086 to 0.103 depending on allocation, putting the risk upper bound near 0.49 to 0.51.
Not comparable with the certification rates prior work reports at its own operating points, which are achieved certifications rather than oracle necessary conditions.

The verdict IS operating-point dependent above the crossing: oracle acceptance for the QLoRA system reaches 0.187 at a target risk of 0.40 and 0.316 at 0.45. The claim is that the frozen target is not a specially unlucky choice, not that no operating point behaves differently.
The frozen headline target remains 0.20 and no certificate exists at any other point.
Scoped to in-domain RAMS and the frozen vLLM 4-bit serving stack.

Model-, score- and task-specific, not a statement about structured extraction. The bound (mu-alpha)/(1-alpha) forbids nothing at alpha = 0.20 for a task at mu = 0.033, and permits up to 80.5% acceptance at mu = 0.356 - both figures 2606.29054 reports for its own extraction and NER datasets (docs/frontier-check/findings.md, re-verified 2026-07-22). So a 20% target is NOT EXCLUDED on structured extraction at those base risks; not being forbidden by a necessary condition is not achievability, and that paper finds certification practical only at alpha = 0.30-0.40 on its own tasks. What is measured here is that THIS model with THIS score on THIS task could not - and NOT because of mu alone, which at 0.6071 still permits 49.1% acceptance. Infeasibility here is overdetermined by base risk, ranking and the finite-sample penalty together (corrected 2026-08-03, review finding F1: an earlier wording said 'at mu = 0.6071 cannot' and 'demonstrably not out of reach', which are the two halves of that finding in one sentence).
